newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura won't confirm board resignation report.
newsitem.headline: Nomura won't confirm board resignation report.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd said it would not confirm media reports on Tuesday that its president and other directors with voting rights would resign to take responsibility for a recent scandal linking it to "sokaiya" racketeers.
"We will not confirm the reports," a Nomura spokesman said.
Kyodo news agency, quoting industry sources, said the president and all nine directors with voting rights would soon step down to take responsibility for the scandal.
Kyodo quoted the sources as saying that president Masashi Suzuki, five vice presidents and four senior managing directors would step down.
Some directors who do not have voting rights will also resign, it said.
The resignations will be announced by the end of this week, it said.
Mass-circulation daily Yomiuri Shimbun said in its Tuesday edition that Nomura may decide on the resignations at a meeting of top management to be held on Tuesday.
